services_shape: one patient with one therapist at a time, each visit with a set length; every new problem starts with an evaluation by a physical therapist; the evaluation sets the plan of care (how many visits a week, for how many weeks), and those visits are booked as a series with the patient's own yes, or one at a time
questions_before_times: for you, or for your child (a parent or guardian books)
a new problem or after surgery (an evaluation), or a visit from your plan of care
a doctor's referral or prescription for therapy: yes (from whom) or no
a health plan (its name only), Medicare, Medicaid, or paying yourself
from a work injury or a car accident: no, a work injury, or a car accident
days and times that suit you
safety_stop: chest pain, trouble breathing, or stroke signs (sudden weakness, a drooping face, slurred speech)
after surgery: a hot or swollen calf, a fever, or a red or leaking wound
a fall with a new injury, or a sudden loss of feeling or control
first_steps: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
The surgeon's protocol and surgery notes
A written price estimate for self-pay patients
The plan's OK for the visits after the evaluation
license: always: each physical therapist and each physical therapist assistant holds their own active license from the state's physical therapy board
staff_skills: physical therapists: evaluations, progress re-checks, the plan of care, and every visit; assistants: follow-up visits only, under a therapist's plan of care; dry needling only by a therapist trained for it; only people cleared for home visits go to homes
messages_never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the surgery, the plan, the reason, the results or the therapist's name at the clinic (at home, the therapist's name stays, for the door check)
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
